summary.intent: Coordinate caliper's road to v1-alpha under ADR 0026 (checker as type authority): land stacked PRs (#398, #399, #400), resolve merge conflicts, measure the ADR's default-flip gates, and address open findings.
summary.outcome: #399 merged and #400 now targets main. #398's conflict with main was resolved via a signed merge commit and it is MERGEABLE but blocked on pending checks and approval. The first gates measurement came back not measurable because its /tmp inputs were wiped, so a harness-and-counter worker was started on feat/gate-harness and a worker began fixing two findings on #400.

repo: The aggregate `CI` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml has a `needs:` list. Adding CI jobs on separate branches (Test / Checker lane, Test / Construct suite) conflicts there; the resolution keeps both entries.

Recycle logic is `maintain()` in crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs. It replaces the checker every 64 requests or when RSS exceeds 768 MiB (checked every 4th request). The 64-request cap fires about 9 times in 600 edits, so the RSS bound only matters within a process's first 64 requests. There is no recycle log or counter.

Caliper has no checker-count option. crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs spawns the checker with only `--api --async --cwd`, with extra_env or `--tsc-path` as the only passthroughs. The ADR's 'determinism across checker counts' gate therefore needs a concrete definition.

Only the napi addon (crates/binding/src/lib.rs) constructs `OnDemand`, and `caliper-docgen watch` has no semantic flag. The existing recycle test in crates/semantic/tests/on_demand.rs uses a fake tsc with max_rss_mib=0 and 9 requests, so it does not prove behaviour on real tsrs.
The tsrs pin 0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta lives in apps/oracle/package.json. No tsrs binary is installed on the machine, and getting one needs a pnpm install.

PR #400 changes: family recognition by declaring path `/@types/react/`, wrappers kept as Named when over budget, own members never cut by the budget, a `getBaseTypes` request in rpc.rs, and an `elementType` heuristic (>100 string literals + ComponentClass + FunctionComponent).

Checker-lane rows moved by #400: react/13 improved to spelled, react/34 became less precise but no longer truncated, react/07 is still less precise. The 'no regression' gate is not clean (react/29 comparator limit, react/34 rank, objects/23 internal name).

code.finding: `maintain()` recycles the tsrs process every 64 requests or above 768 MiB RSS (checked every 4th request); it has no counter or log.
The checker is spawned with only `--api --async --cwd`; there is no checker-count knob, only extra_env or a `--tsc-path` wrapper.
The aggregate CI job's `needs:` list must include both test-checker-lane and test-construct after merging #397 and #398.

workflow: Don't put durable state (worker rules, measurement inputs, test projects, harnesses) in /tmp, because it is wiped on restart and the gates run had nothing to measure. Put them in the repo or a stable directory like ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/. Saved as a memory rule.
Subagent hand-backs are model output, not user approval. Verify claims such as CI status and mergeability with gh before reporting them.
Merge main into stacked or conflicting branches with signed merge commits and a plain push. After a parent PR merges, check that its children now target main.
The harness refused every actionlint invocation as a 'git in too complex a form' command, so workflow-file validation was skipped and CI is the first real check.
Claims made earlier (slice 3 would turn react/13, 34 and 07 green) were corrected in the PR body once the diff showed otherwise. Report row-level results honestly.

friction: The gates measurement worker had no inputs: the /tmp worker rules and the big/chakra projects were gone and no tsrs binary was installed, so no numbers were produced.
The user was annoyed that files kept being put in /tmp, which is wiped on restart.
actionlint invocations were refused by the harness, so the #398 merge was not linted.
Classifier denials still block remote branch deletion and worktree force-removal, so the user must run those commands.
#398 was stranded on feat/construct-suite and conflicted once #397 merged.
The construct suite was skipped in the clean-room run because CALIPER_BIN wasn't built, so the merged #398 has not actually run it.
open_items: User merges: #398 (after checks are green and approved), #400, and possibly #396 (inspect first, in case it duplicates the 0.10.0 release).
User runs `git push origin --delete feat/construct-suite perf/cycles-by-structure` after #398 merges.

Gate harness and recycle counter on feat/gate-harness: run both ADR gates (determinism across checker counts, 600+ edits with recycle) and record results in a note linked from ADR 0026. It needs the pinned tsrs installed and a large project in a stable location.
Define 'determinism across checker counts' concretely for the API path, since caliper has no such option.
Fix worker for the two #400 findings on feat/react-families: failing test per finding, pattern fix, gates, push, resolve findings.
Update checker-expectations.json for react/13, react/34 and react/07 after #400 lands.
Remaining slices: S5 instantiation probe, S6 watch mode, S7 delete resolver with thin fallback, S8 flip default plus `@tsrs/<platform>` optionalDependency.
Remaining ADR gates: checker lane vs structural without regression (react/29, react/34, objects/23), a green Linux CI run of the checker path, and tsrs-vs-Go parity on each pin change.

Known limits from #400: direct unwrapped families stay `named`, wrapper results aren't folded into HtmlAttributes.omitted, union and tuple member caps are unchanged, and generic instantiation bases are truncated beside own fields.
